sections.value:
# Security verdict, PR #299 (F248 + F247), round 1, head 7a6e632b

Result: PASS-WITH-NOTES. No finding blocks. All checks were by direct reading in this seat, with read-only probes. Nothing was built, nothing was run with --apply, and the daemon was not touched.

## Q1: Linux uid classification
- The foreign skip cannot license deleting a live socket in this user's tmux dir in normal use. `socket_verdict` and `lock_verdict` remove only files whose owner is this real uid (`ours()`, tmux_sweep.rs ~194, ~612, ~640). The tmux dir is mode 0700, so only this user or root can create entries in it. A root (euid 0 and fsuid 0) bind makes a root-owned file, which is Unsure and never removed. A `sudo` process is euid/fsuid 0 and binds nothing of ours. A process with euid or fsuid ours counts as ours (`foreign`, ~404).
- Residual cases (Low, not normal use): (a) a socket file of ours whose only holder later becomes euid and fsuid foreign: an inherited listening fd across a setuid exec, an SCM_RIGHTS pass to a root or subordinate-uid process, or a root service that bound with setfsuid(ours) and dropped back; (b) the /proc scan is not atomic, so an fd that moves from an unscanned pid to an already-scanned pid and is then closed at its source within the scan window is missed. A fresh bind is covered by the 10 min YOUNG brake, but an old inherited socket is not; (c) holders that /proc/<pid>/fd cannot show: in-flight SCM_RIGHTS fds, io_uring fixed files, CLONE_FILES-unshared threads (task/<tid>/fd); (d) a sweep run inside a separate PID namespace that shares /tmp with host processes no longer sees those holders. Before this PR, /proc/net/unix was netns-scoped, not pidns-scoped. None applies to tmux servers started by pij's fixtures.
- Gone mid-scan, then skip: safe against pid reuse. Skips happen only on NotFound. A reused pid is read as the new process (its fds, or EACCES, which makes the read Unknown). An exiting process's fds are closed and hold nothing.
- Availability note: on hosts with `hidepid=1`/`noaccess`, every other user's `status` is unreadable, so each counts as ours, its `fd` read fails with EACCES, and the sweep is always BLOCKED. This fails closed; consider treating EACCES on another user's process as unknown-owner only when `fd` is ours.

## Q2: fake-/proc seam
`own_socket_inodes(proc, uid, only)` and `linux_bound_paths(only)` are private. Production `bound_paths()` hardcodes `/proc` and `None`. No `env::var` reads in tmux_sweep.rs or the binary. argv takes only `--dir`/`--apply`, and `--dir` does not steer the holder read. It is compiled into production but cannot be reached or steered there. PASS.

## Q3: BLOCKED rendering (note S299-N1, Low, hardening)
`Holders::of_bound` renders `path.display()` raw (tmux_sweep.rs ~265–270), and the binary prints it on the `holders: UNKNOWN:` and `stale: unknown; BLOCKED` lines. `decode_lsof_name` turns `\xHH`/`\b`/`\r` back into raw bytes (~498–521), and /proc/net/unix prints paths raw, so an ESC or CR in a bound path reaches the terminal unescaped. The parse-error paths (~438, ~597) use `from_utf8_lossy`, which also keeps control characters. The source is a socket path held by this user's own processes, which is out of scope under C33 (same user), and `unknown_in` already did this before the PR. The PR does widen it from paths in the swept dir to any bound path of ours. Suggest rendering with `{:?}` or `escape_debug`. The pid is numeric, and the Uid text comes from the kernel. C21: no home paths in the diff, commit messages or PR body.

## Q4: F247 justfile (note S299-N2, Low, C33 operator-env)
- No injection: `"$UID"` is one quoted argv word, there is no eval, and the decode is unchanged (`printf -v name '%b'`, matching by `-ef`).
- `$UID` is not tamper-proof on the bash this recipe gets on macOS: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to /bin/bash 3.2, which imports UID (and EUID) from the environment. Repro: `env UID=0 bash -c 'echo $UID'` prints 0, while bash 5 refuses (readonly). Numeric spoofs fail closed (`lsof -u 0|1000|99999` exits 1, so the bounce refuses). `lsof -u '^501'` exits 0 with empty output, though, so `UID='^501' just bounce-rs` passes the holder check without the audited PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE message. This needs the operator's own environment, and it grants nothing `PIJ_BOUNCE_LSOF=/usr/bin/true` doesn't already grant, so it is not a block. Cheap hardening: `case $UID in ''|*[!0-9]*) refuse ;; esac` before the launch. PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE handling is unchanged.

## Q5: public-repo checks
No secret or token patterns in the diff. No lockfile or .npmrc change. `git ls-remote origin 'refs/notes/*'` is empty. No home paths in committed text, commit messages or PR body.

## Performance and cost (security view only)
The Linux read moves from one file read to a /proc walk: one `status` read plus one `fd` readdir and readlinks per process, in-process, once per manual run, with no launch. F247 removes one `id` launch per refusal-path bounce. The performance role owns the measurements.
